subject: Re: Dedicated capacity proposal – GPU pool sizing & executive discount request
messages:
From: Elena Park <elena@orionai.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@orionai.com
Date: Thu, 25 Jun 2026 15:20:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity question: committed pool size & pricing flexibility

Hi Dylan,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the latency numbers look very promising for our inference workload. We have an internal procurement window opening in July and I wanted to confirm a couple of items before we prepare a recommendation: 

- We expect steady production traffic that would justify a committed pool of ~8 A100 GPUs (peak burst to 12) for the initial rollout. Can Redwood provide guidance on throughput guarantees (tokens/sec or concurrent request targets) for that pool profile?
- Pricing: your term sheet shows list pricing for Dedicated. We have a competing offer from another vendor that includes a 20% effective discount if we commit for 12 months. Will Redwood consider a pricing exception or credits to match that band for strategic customers?
- Contractual asks: 99.9% availability SLA on serving nodes, and a 90-day migration credit if we need to scale down in the first year.

I've attached the RFP spec and our internal sizing notes. Please let me know if you need anything else to accelerate internal approvals.

Best,
Elena Park
Head of ML Ops, Orion AI

Attachments: OrionAI_RFP_Specs.pdf (pdf)
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Park <elena@orionai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 26 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity question: committed pool size & pricing flexibility

Hi Elena — great questions, and thanks for the RFP. I'll summarize and propose next steps: 

- Throughput guarantees: for an 8x A100 reserved pool we typically size for ~1,200 concurrent token-generating sessions (mixed request sizes) with 95th percentile tail latency targets around 150-250ms for short-form prompts. We can run a quick synthetic workload based on your request/response distribution to give a more precise tokens/sec SLT.
- Pricing exceptions: we do have the ability to offer account-level credits and limited-term discounts for strategic commitments. To evaluate we need: competitor offer terms (published or redacted), expected committed term (12 vs 24 months), and whether Orion would take a Dedicated + burst credits add-on.
- SLA and migration credit: 99.9% availability is in scope; migration credits are considered but need exec approval when paired with deep discounts.

Requested next steps:
1) Elena: confirm 12-month vs 24-month commit and whether you want burst headroom to 12 GPUs.
2) Elena: share competitor redacted term sheet (just pricing bands is fine).
3) Internally: I'll pull Karthik and Marissa into pricing discussion and request an exception if we need to match 20% off.

I'll loop in Sergio for the throughput verification and Marissa for commercial approval.

Thanks,
Dylan
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 27 Jun 2026 10:55:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity question: committed pool size & pricing flexibility

Looping in a quick technical note on throughput sizing:

- Baseline: 8x A100 (40GB) configured with our continuous-batching runtime should sustain ~2.5M tokens/min aggregate assuming mixed short-to-medium prompts and KV cache enabled. That maps roughly to the concurrent session estimate Dylan quoted.
- Burst behavior: we can allow soft bursts to 12 GPUs via reserved burst credits; this adds a marginal incremental monthly cost (can be modeled into the term sheet).
- Guardrails: if Orion's workload is heavily long-context or generates large token outputs, we should consider a 10–15% uplift in pool size. We can validate after a 48-hour replay test using Orion's sample traces.

I'll prepare a short runbook for the throughput validation and attach our test harness.

—Sergio
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 29 Jun 2026 08:34:00 -0700
Subject: Discount exception request: Orion AI (DEAL-4832)

Team,

Dylan flagged that Orion is asking us to match an effective 20% discount if they commit for 12 months. Context: strategic AI infra customer, potential logo in financial services vertical via their partners, and likely expansion to Dedicated in EU next year.

Request: approve a one-time commercial exception for a 15% list discount plus $75k in non-recurring onboarding credits (applied over first 3 months) — contingent on:
- Signed 12-month reserved commit for 8 GPUs (with burst to 12)
- Standard SLA (99.9%) and SLOs in the Dedicated addendum
- No additional custom indemnities beyond our standard enterprise terms

If we want to match 20% we need an exec uplift (Evelyn) because that materially reduces unit economics for the first year.

Please reply with approve/reject and brief rationale.

Marissa
Director, Commercial Sales
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discount exception request: Orion AI (DEAL-4832)

Thanks for the context. I approve Marissa's proposed commercial exception: 15% discount + $75k onboarding credits for a 12-month committed 8 GPU pool with burst to 12, subject to:
- Legal to approve standard Dedicated addendum (no custom T&Cs)
- Finance to validate revenue recognition for credits and ensure ARR commitments are captured
- Include a 90-day migration credit clause as a capped credit (equivalent to up to 25% of one month's committed fee) — not uncapped.

Dylan: please relay the offer to Orion, request the redacted competitor terms for audit, and push to get signature this month. If Orion insists on 20% we will consider incremental credits instead of deeper discount to preserve list integrity.

Evelyn
VP, GTM Operations
